chapter: Trumpeters he admired and the Ellington near-miss
title: What might have been: Ellington's trumpet features and Jones's cold feet
summary: He imagines what Ellington would have written for him as he did for Rex Stewart and Cootie in "Tooting Through the Roof" and "Boy Meets Horn"; he admits he had cold feet about those aloof men.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, that's interesting, Jonah. It's a pity you didn't, you know. But I mean you don't know what all might come of it.
No, I don't know what it would have been.
But it would have been interesting.
I think that maybe it would have been a thing like -- because you know how he would do, he would put things behind you, like this guy --
Look what he did for Rex Stewart.
Sure. Who would ever have thought Rex would fit in there.
The trumpets and all that. Extraordinary. What was that --
Yeah, 'Tooting Through the Roof.' Oh, goodness, that's -- him and Cootie. And then you had them playing 'Trumpet No End', which was, 'Blue Skies.' Had about five trumpets in there.
I mean who but Ellington could have brought
It was a beautiful thing. Well, that's the way it goes. You see --
But it's a pity in a way, if you'd just even spent two or three years with him --
Oh, yeah, I'd have loved that. I'd have loved it till today, you know, but that day, to tell you the truth, I had cold feet, you know.
Because these was guys that I didn't know how good -- I was just getting to know them, since I was playing Buffalo, that they were coming in there every year, to play the theater.
And they were funny guys, too.
Oh, yeah, they were different types of cats, different types of cats.
I mean they weren't outgoing guys and they all had their own little worlds going.
